the-submission-gate-comes-out.why: The second half of the owner's decision, removed. Without it a file submits with no date of birth and no nationality, and the sanctions check then runs on a NAME ALONE — which `buildScreeningSubjects` records in its own header as *"the single largest source of false positives"* against ~19,000 entries. Planted, **`refuses a submit without either field, naming the one that is missing`** dies on `expected 422 "Unprocessable Entity", got 201 "Created"`, and the six tests beside it pass — including the corporate one, which is how the plant shows the gate was individual-only rather than absent.

the-refusal-lists-the-rule-instead-of-th.to: `KYCRecord ${id}: cannot submit an individual's file without dateOfBirth and nationality.
the-refusal-lists-the-rule-instead-of-th.why: The owner's instruction was *"refusing by naming the missing field"*, and this is the version that names the RULE instead. A reader whose record already carries a nationality is told to supply one, so they go looking for a field that is already filled — which is how a correct refusal becomes an unactionable one. Planted, the gate test fails on `expected '…without dateOfBirth and nationality.…' not to contain 'without dateOfBirth and nationality'`. **AND THE ASSERTION BEHIND IT IS A CORRECTION FROM THE RUN**: my first version was a page-wide `not.toContain('nationality')`, which fails on the CORRECT message — the refusal explains the rule after naming the field, and the explanation mentions both. Scoped to the slot, it distinguishes the two; page-wide it could not.

the-correction-stops-re-screening.why: THE PLANT FOR THE PROPERTY THE WHOLE STRIKE RESTS ON. The owner struck her own 2026-09-28 deferral because the controlled path *"records who changed it and when, keeps the encrypted before and after, demands a written reason, and RE-SCREENES"*. Remove the re-screen and the two fields become an unguarded edit of a screening identifier — exactly what she refused in September. Planted, **`corrects both fields, records the before and after, and re-screens`** dies on `expected null not to be null` for `newScreeningResultId`, which is the right failure: the correction row is what records that the check happened. `customer-identifier-correction.inventory.spec.ts` is deliberately NOT what catches this one — it checks that the caller SPELLS `this.screening.run`, and this plant keeps the spelling while gutting the call, which is why a behavioural assertion is needed beside the sweep.

the-reason-becomes-optional.why: The contact route's reason is optional and its own comment says why — *"a mandatory justification on fixing a phone number is friction on the commonest case"* — and that same comment says of the identifiers *"there the reason is part of the record the AMLU requires to be retained, and it will be mandatory"*. This is the plant for that distinction collapsing. **CORRECTED TWICE FROM THE RUN, and the first correction is the one that matters.** My `why` first claimed the floor test would still fail on the SHORT reason; it did not — **the plant killed NOTHING, 7 of 7 passed**, because `@IsOptional()` skips only an ABSENT value and both of that test's bodies CARRY a reason. So the mandatory reason had no observer anywhere in the suite, and an assertion sending no reason at all was added for it. **AND THE SECOND CORRECTION IS A FINDING IN OUR FAVOUR**: with that assertion the plant fails **`expected 400 "Bad Request", got 500 "Internal Server Error"`** — not a 400. `CustomerIdentifierCorrection.reason` is NOT NULL and this path (unlike the contact one) supplies no default, so an absent reason cannot be RECORDED at all; the DTO is the usable guard and the column is a structural backstop. A 500 is loud, which is the right direction for a guard to fail in, and it is why the recorded consequence is *the request dies* rather than *an empty reason is stored*.

the-trim-comes-off-the-length-check.why: The DSR intake's defect, one batch later, on a field where it matters more. Without the transform, `@Length(10, …)` counts TEN SPACES as length 10 and the correction is recorded with an empty reason — on the row the AMLU requires retained as *"the verification mechanism and actions taken"*. ORDER is the point: `@Transform` runs before the validator, which is why it lives on the DTO and the service does not trim at all. Planted, **`refuses a reason below the declaration floor, and whitespace does not satisfy it`** dies on `expected 400 "Bad Request", got 200 "OK"` for the ten-space body, while the nine-character half still passes — the two halves separated so the failure says which.

a-no-change-correction-is-accepted.why: Accepting a correction that changes nothing writes a row reading *corrected dateOfBirth from 1990-01-01 to 1990-01-01* into the one table that exists to be justifiable, and re-screens for an answer that cannot differ. The contact path has no equivalent check because re-sending a phone number costs nothing; here it costs a false evidence row and a wasted provider call. **CORRECTED FROM THE RUN: this plant and `a-company-may-carry-a-date-of-birth` originally killed the SAME test with the identical message, so the output could not say which refusal had gone** — one-at-a-time is pointless if the failure cannot name WHICH, the lesson the DSR intake's three refusals paid for one batch ago. The test was split; this plant now fails **`refuses a correction in which every value sent is already on the record`** with `expected 422, got 200`, and the corporate test beside it passes.

a-company-may-carry-a-date-of-birth.why: A company has no date of birth or nationality of its own — `buildScreeningSubjects` says so in as many words, and passing the company's own null there is *"correct, not a gap"*, because those facts belong to the natural persons behind it and the UBO subjects carry them. Accepting them on a corporate customer writes two columns nothing screens. Planted, **`refuses a corporate customer — a company has no date of birth of its own`** fails with `expected 422, got 200` while the no-change test passes — which it could not do before the split, because the two refusals shared a test and reported the same message. **And the WEB half of this same property is guarded from an unexpected direction**: the pre-existing `shows an individual no corporate fields, and a company no national ID` asserts that the strings *Date of birth* and *Nationality* are ABSENT within `main` for a company — so the identifier control leaking onto a corporate screen fails that test too, found while fixing the strict-mode violation my own control's label created.

the-corrected-values-enter-the-immutable.why: THE SAME PDPL DECISION AS THE DSR INTAKE'S, and the plant that looks most reasonable of the eight — a correction history that cannot say what the value WAS is a poor history, which is exactly the argument the contact path uses to record the ADDRESS before and after. The difference is the LOG rather than the column: `AuditLogEntry` is immutable by trigger, so a date of birth written there is personal data an ERASURE REQUEST CAN NEVER REACH, while the Customer row and the correction row can both be reached. (The contact path's own reason — *writing the plaintext would defeat the encrypted column* — does NOT apply here: neither field is encrypted on `Customer`.) Planted, **`corrects both fields, records the before and after, and re-screens`** dies on the snapshot assertion — `expected '…"dateOfBirth":"1988-06-21"…' not to contain '1988-06-21'` — which is the half of the DSR plant that had no instrument at all, built here because this time there was something to assert.

the-screen-stops-enforcing-the-reason-fl.why: A screen must not send a request it already knows will be refused. Without the floor the button enables the moment a date is typed, the officer presses it, and the server answers 400 about a field they did not think they were filling in wrongly. Planted, **`records an identifier correction, with the reason floor enforced before the request`** dies on the NINE-character assertion — `expect(locator).toBeDisabled()` — and that is why the test types nine characters rather than none: an empty form is disabled because no identifier is filled, so a test that only checked the empty state would pass against this plant.

the-control-appears-on-a-company.why: The server refuses a corporate customer with a 422, so a control offered there is a button whose only outcome is a refusal — the shape `docs/frontend-ux-directive.md` forbids (*a control a role cannot use does not exist on their screen*), met one axis over: not a permission but a customer type. Planted, it kills **TWO** tests rather than the one it was written for, and the second is the find. **`offers no identifier correction on a CORPORATE customer, while the contact one stays`** dies on `toHaveCount(0)` finding one, its anchor (the CONTACT control, visible) still passing — which is what proves the absence was measured against a hydrated page rather than an empty one. **AND the pre-existing `shows an individual no corporate fields, and a company no national ID` dies too**, because it asserts that the strings *Date of birth* and *Nationality* are ABSENT within `main` for a company, and this control's own label carries both. That second observer was found while fixing the strict-mode violation my control's label created in that same test — so the ambiguity this change introduced is also what made that test a second guard on this property. **2 failed, 22 passed.**
